title: Redis Software REST API quick start
summary: Redis Software REST API quick start

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Redis Software includes a REST API that allows you to automate certain tasks. This article shows you how to send a request to the Redis Software REST API.

sections.title: Fundamentals
sections.text:
No matter which method you use to send API requests, there are a few common concepts to remember.

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [Authentication](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api#authentication) | Use [Basic Auth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication) with your cluster username (email) and password |
| [Ports](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api#ports) | All calls are made to port 9443 by default |
| [Versions](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api#versions) | Specify the version in the request [URI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier) |
| [Headers](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api#headers) | `Accept` and `Content-Type` should be `application/json` |
| [Response types and error codes](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api#response-types-and-error-codes) | A response of `200 OK` means success; otherwise, the request failed due to an error |  

For more information, see [Redis Software REST API](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api/).

sections.title: cURL example requests
sections.text:
[cURL](https://curl.se/) is a command-line tool that allows you to send HTTP requests from a terminal.

You can use the following options to build a cURL request:

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| -X     | Method (GET, PUT, PATCH, POST, or DELETE) |
| -H     | Request header, can be specified multiple times |
| -u     | Username and password information |
| -d     | JSON data for PUT or POST requests |
| -F     | Form data for PUT or POST requests, such as for the [`POST /v1/modules`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api/requests/modules/#post-module) or [`POST /v2/modules`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api/requests/modules/#post-module-v2) endpoint |
| -k     | Turn off SSL  verification |
| -i     | Show headers and status code as well as the response body |

See the [cURL documentation](https://curl.se/docs/) for more information.

sections.title: PUT request
sections.text:
Once you have the database ID, you can use [PUT `/v1/bdbs/`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/references/rest-api/requests/bdbs/#put-bdbs) to update the configuration of the database.

For example, you can pass the database `uid` 1 as a URL parameter and use the `-d` option to specify the new `name` when you send the request. This changes the database's `name` from `tr01` to `database1`:

sections.title: Client examples
sections.text:
You can also use client libraries to make API requests in your preferred language.

To follow these examples, you need:

- A [Redis Software](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/installing-upgrading/quickstarts/redis-enterprise-software-quickstart) node
- Python 3 and the [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests/) Python library
- [node.js](https://nodejs.dev/) and [node-fetch](https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-fetch)

import json
import requests

# Required connection information - replace with your host, port, username, and password
host = "[host]"
port = "[port]"
username = "[username]"
password = "[password]"

# Get the list of databases using GET /v1/bdbs
bdbs_uri = "https://{}:{}/v1/bdbs".format(host, port)

print("GET {}".format(bdbs_uri))
get_resp = requests.get(bdbs_uri,
        auth = (username, password),
        headers = { "accept" : "application/json" },
        verify = False)

print("{} {}".format(get_resp.status_code, get_resp.reason))
for header in get_resp.headers.keys():
    print("{}: {}".format(header, get_resp.headers[header]))

print("\n" + json.dumps(get_resp.json(), indent=4))

# Rename all databases using PUT /v1/bdbs
for bdb in get_resp.json():
    uid = bdb["uid"] # Get the database ID from the JSON response

    put_uri = "{}/{}".format(bdbs_uri, uid)
    new_name = "database{}".format(uid)
    put_data = { "name" : new_name }

    print("PUT {} {}".format(put_uri, json.dumps(put_data)))

    put_resp = requests.put(put_uri,
        data = json.dumps(put_data),
        auth = (username, password),
        headers = { "content-type" : "application/json" },
        verify = False)

    print("{} {}".format(put_resp.status_code, put_resp.reason))
    for header in put_resp.headers.keys():
        print("{}: {}".format(header, put_resp.headers[header]))

    print("\n" + json.dumps(put_resp.json(), indent=4))
